variants.label: top room trimmed, right-edge pipes slid in, bottom room's ports moved to its right wall
variants.architecture: Three steps. (1) The top room's six empty right columns are trimmed; the one read this broke -- row 4 column 24, which preferred the I pipe by a single step -- is fixed by bringing the I pipe in through the BOTTOM wall at column 14 instead of the left wall (solving the room's six reads as distance inequalities gives a feasible window of columns 12-24). (2) The two right-edge pipes, left 6 cells longer by the trim, have their verticals slid into the freed columns: width 46 -> 40 and both pipes end up SHORTER than they began (91->87, 67->63). (3) The bottom room has exactly one incoming and one outgoing pipe, so resolution is trivial and the wall is free to choose: both are re-routed through its RIGHT wall into the freed columns, which deletes rows 43-45 entirely.

variants.label: mechanical squeeze of empty rows/columns
variants.architecture: Whole-program squeeze via src/littleman/alexey_squeeze.py (rows only -- the column pass breaks it 2/7): every row made only of ' ' and '|', and every column made only of ' ' and '-', is deleted. No room re-laid, no pipe re-routed. Shortens each room interior and each vertical pipe it crosses by one cell; the walk is identical apart from being shorter, which is why ticks fall too.
variants.verdict: TEAM BEST for memory: 91,372,248 -> 87,493,514 (1.04x). Most of the gain on the large programs is ticks, not area -- the surviving pipes got shorter.

note: Alexey research line for memory. memory_03 is the current best at 75,823,407 (40x43), down from the 87,493,514 baseline.
